clue.text: Maids terrified to take a risk. Bad luck!

indicators.note: someone terrified is thrown into disorder, so the preceding word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
to venture is to take a risk

explanation.surface: Frightened housemaids gamble on something, and it goes badly for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A misadventure is an unlucky mishap, so the exclamation of bad luck stands for it as a near synonym.

clue.text: Warlike Roman poet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: suited to or connected with war
second meaning: the Latin writer of epigrams of the first century AD

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one warlike poet, but the adjective and the poet's name are separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to fighting, and Martial was a celebrated Latin epigrammatist from Spain.

clue.text: Keep some evasive action up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the run of letters is found at the start of evasive

explanation.surface: An instruction to maintain some dodging manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks EVAS out of 'evasive', and 'up' turns it round in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To save something is to keep it, as in saving money or keeping it aside for later.

clue.text: Fearless leader of diehards takes a call

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
to give someone a ring is to make a phone call

explanation.surface: The boldest of a stubborn band picks up the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: A ring is British colloquial for a telephone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring describes someone bold and unafraid of danger, a close synonym of fearless.

clue.text: Relief energy chaps imported to Orient

indicators.note: something imported is brought inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the Orient is the East
E is the physics symbol for energy
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Bringing power and men into the Far East to ease things.
explanation.walkthrough: Energy and chaps join first, and that pair is what gets imported into the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Easement means a lessening of pain or discomfort, so it is a dictionary synonym for relief.

clue.text: Set fire to land used for night processions

parts.note: to torch something is to set it alight
to light is to land or settle, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: Burning a stretch of ground to illuminate a parade after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' is the verb, as in alighting, not a piece of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Torchlight is illumination from flaming torches, the traditional light carried by marchers in parades after dark.

clue.text: Scolded about extremes of evil in the family

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to rate is an old word for to scold

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer in the household gets told off for his wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: To rate is an archaic verb meaning to berate, still met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives are people in the same family, so being related means connected by kinship, an adjectival phrase match.

clue.text: A warning: very small amount's planned in advance

parts.note: taken as written
the shout golfers give to warn of a ball in flight
a thought means a little, as in 'a thought too salty'

explanation.surface: A tiny cautionary note turns out to have been prepared beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the word in 'malice aforethought'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforethought means premeditated, deliberately considered beforehand, as in the legal phrase for intentional harm.

clue.text: Always in fashion, therefore very useful

indicators.note: in fashion is read as 'in the manner of' the following words, which carry the answer inside them
useful here says the two words are put to use for the answer, which they hold in their own letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of therefore and the start of very

explanation.surface: Something always fashionable, and so very handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fashion' tempts as a definition of stylish; instead it and 'useful' point into 'therefore very', where the answer runs across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Forever means for all time, so it can stand for always, as in 'he is forever complaining'.

clue.text: Too much not wholly reliable addition

indicators.note: not wholly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: sure means reliable, as in a sure bet
plus is an addition, an extra

explanation.surface: An unreliable extra makes things excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an amount left over beyond what is needed, an excess, so it means too much.

clue.text: What one does automatically to support wildlife

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
nature covers the wild animals and plants of the world

explanation.surface: Backing conservation is something a person does without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase: the thing one does automatically.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit so ingrained it feels instinctive is called second nature, an idiom for behaviour done without conscious thought.

clue.text: Check fall in one's hearing

indicators.note: in someone's hearing means as heard, so go by how the word is spoken

parts.note: a fall of rain; spoken the same as the strap for a horse

explanation.surface: A shower is audible nearby while someone checks.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or hold back, so rein as a verb means check, from the horse's leather strap.

clue.text: Put machine for repair without insisting on it

indicators.note: something put in for repair gets taken apart and rebuilt, so letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sends a device off to be fixed in a low-key, unpushy way.
explanation.definitionFit: Unemphatic means said or done mildly, lacking force or stress, which is acting without pressing a point.

clue.text: Study stream running alongside

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a current is a stream of water or air

explanation.surface: Examining a brook that flows beside the path.
explanation.definitionFit: Concurrent events happen at the same time, running in parallel with each other, so the phrase matches.

clue.text: Fat everyone has to lug round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: to tow is to haul or drag
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Every overweight person must carry their bulk about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like an adjective for the people but is the noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, used for candles and soap, so it is a specific kind of fat.

clue.text: Hopeless redundancies case lost — never even mounted

indicators.note: hopeless suggests the letters are in a hopeless muddle, so they are to be rearranged
lost tells us the letters of the word case go missing from the jumble

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
letters taken out of the fodder, as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy note about job cuts in which some legal case was lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters C, A, S, E out of REDUNDANCIES, leaving R D U N D N I E, and rearrange those to spell UNRIDDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that has never once been mounted by a rider is one that has stayed unridden.

clue.text: Old beast raving mad? Not so

indicators.note: raving means wild and deranged, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the ancient creature stark mad? Apparently not.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastodon is an extinct elephant-like mammal, an animal from prehistoric times, so it is an ancient beast.

clue.text: Pub measure, one put before an expert on glasses

parts.note: an Optic is the measuring device on an upturned spirit bottle in a British bar
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barman measures out a drink and sets it before a connoisseur of glassware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glasses' suggests drinks at the pub but means spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician tests eyesight and prescribes or supplies spectacles, so is a specialist in eyewear.

clue.text: N African city constructed from granite

indicators.note: something constructed from materials is assembled anew, so letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A North African town built out of hard stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a Moroccan port on the Strait of Gibraltar, so it is a city in northern Africa.

clue.text: No rash moves from her!

indicators.note: moves means the letters shift position into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cautious woman who never acts impulsively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' is the definition: any woman's name fits a female pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharon is a female first name, and the pronoun stands in for some particular woman.

clue.text: Score in ball-game with better finish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a full run scored in the bat-and-ball game ...
second meaning: more round, more polished or complete

explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British children's game like baseball, where a completed circuit of the bases scores one point.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a point in rounders; the comparative adjective means more rounded off, more polished in finish.

clue.text: Party gets vote turning up in lump

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: turning up in a down answer means the letters climb in the opposite direction

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A political party gains ground as the vote swings its way in a chunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless mass or blob of something soft, such as cream, so it is a lump.

clue.text: Producing quota of hereditary material

parts.note: a gene is a unit of inherited material
a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: A biologist manufactures a set share of DNA.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read in reverse: the quota comes after the hereditary material.
explanation.definitionFit: Generation means the act of producing, as in the generation of electricity, matching the gerund.

clue.text: Pursuit from which untold arguments spring

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a courtship, the pursuit of someone's hand
second meaning: a lawsuit, the source of endless legal argument

explanation.walkthrough: The answer also sits in plain view at the end of 'Pursuit', a bonus for the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor pays suit to a lover, and a lawsuit is a court case producing countless legal disputes.

clue.text: Harsh noise from car as petrol runs out

indicators.note: from signals the answer is taken out of the next words
the answer's letters run out partway through petrol, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the letters run from the end of car through as to the start of petrol

explanation.surface: A grating sound from an engine as the fuel tank empties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points inside 'car as petrol', and 'runs out' says the answer stops at the first letter of 'petrol'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a rough grating sound, like a file scraped across wood, so a harsh noise.

clue.text: Shadow on object at the back

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow or shadow them
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A dark shape cast on something behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tail-end describes the rearmost part, so used attributively it means positioned at the back.

clue.text: Famous swimmer's thinner, having eaten last of food

indicators.note: having eaten something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within

parts.note: leaner means thinner

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A celebrated swimmer has slimmed down despite eating.
explanation.walkthrough: LEANER swallows D. In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander of Greek legend swam across the Hellespont each night to his lover Hero, and drowned one stormy night.

clue.text: Material thesis's author may need for his task

definitions.text: Material thesis's author may need for his task

parts.words: Material thesis's author may need for his task
parts.note: surface reading: the research sources a doctoral student must gather; setter's reading: the sheets anyone composing a paper of the academic kind writes on

explanation.surface: A doctoral student gathers sources needed for a dissertation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' suggests research content, but it is the physical stationery; and a thesis is itself a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper is stationery sheets for writing on, the literal material anyone composing a long document needs.
